Commentary.Commentary: We are back for New Zealand's reply. The players of South Africa are going through their fielding drills as the two umpires make their way out to the middle. Neil Brand with a pep talk in the Proteas huddle before they take their places on the field. It will be Devon Conway and Tom Latham to open the innings for New Zealand. Dane Paterson will start with the new ball for the visitors. Away we go...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

The bowling from the Kiwis was brilliant as they stuck to a perfect channel and bombarded back-to-back deliveries in the perfect areas. Rachin Ravindra was brilliant as he took 3 while William O'Rourke took four and the rest all chipped in with wickets as well. With the visitors scoring a mere 242 in their first innings the Kiwis would be once again aiming to bat long and inflict a massive lead on them.

The visitors were good with the bat but would be gutted on the way a few of their batters got out and threw up a good start that they got. After starting with 220 for 6 overnight the resistance of Shaun von Berg gave up early in the day as he succumbed to William O'Rourke and the tail then followed him in no time. Apart from Clyde Fortuin and Keegan Petersen everybody chipped in with a few but failed to capitalize on the starts they got. Ruan de Swardt was by far the best batter for the visitors as he implemented himself better than anybody else on the opponents and scored 64 runs.
We come to a close of the Proteas inning as they have been bundled out on 242 by the Kiwis.

The ball comes on slower than he expected and he ends up slicing it high in the air off the bottom half of the bat. It goes up only as far as second slip as where Tom Latham settles under it and dives forward to take the catch safely. William O'Rourke finishes with 4 wickets and South Africa have been bowled out for 242 in their first innings.

On the other hand, South Africa had a decent opening day. The visitors were better than what they had offered since landing in New Zealand. The Proteas enjoyed a good spell with the bat and a massive credit for that goes to the way Ruan de Swardt has batted. All the batters barring Clyde Fortuin and Keegan Petersen got starts but threw their wickets away and did not go on to score big one and this might come back to haunt the visitors.

New Zealand will be happy that they did not allow South Africa to run away towards a big total and kept on taking wickets regularly. The partnership between Ruan de Swardt and Shaun von Berg has looked threatening though as both have played solidly. Ruan de Swardt in particular has looked more compact and would be eyeing a three-figure mark after going past his half-century yesterday. New Zealand would be looking to break this partnership early on in the day and not let the Proteas build up another big one with the bat.
Hello and welcome to our coverage of Day 2 of the second Test between New Zealand and South Africa.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ....

Right then, as the first day's play draws to a close, neither side will be too unhappy about how the proceedings went for them. With the second new ball only 9 overs old, New Zealand will look to make good use of the early movement on offer on Day 2 and take the remaining 4 wickets and bat when the conditions will likely be the same as Day 1. As for South Africa, the onus will be on this pair to see off that first hour and bat for as long as possible to stretch the first-inning total close to 300 at the very least. Day 2 will begin at 3.30 am IST (10 pm GMT, the previous day), but you can join us earlier for the build-up. Until then, take care and goodbye!

As for New Zealand, patience was the theme of the day for them. They were patient throughout and kept the Proteas batters in check on this opening day. Matt Henry set the tone for the Kiwis with a wicket in his first over, thanks to a one-handed grab from Glenn Phillips. It was the debutant, William O'Rourke, who gave them the second breakthrough before Neil Wagner used his short-ball ploy to get in on the wickets column. Introduced early in the second session, Rachin Ravindra exploited the conditions and went bang, bang, in successive overs. Just as David Bedingham was starting to trouble New Zealand, Rachin struck again to nip him in the bud after Tea. Having had South Africa on the ropes at 150-6, the hosts would have fancied themselves go on to bowl them out and bat at some point in the day, but they faced stiff resistance from Ruan de Swardt and Shaun von Berg. Credit to the Proteas pair for keeping the Kiwi bowlers at bay, and as a result, New Zealand had only six wickets to show for their efforts.

SESSION SUMMARY -  93 runs, 33 overs and 1 wicket. End of an engrossing day of Test cricket! The first two sessions on this opening day went New Zealand's way, but the third session belonged well and truly to South Africa. Earlier in the day, after Neil Brand called it right, he had no hesitation in batting first on a green top. The visitors were rocked early as Clyde Fortuin fell for a golden duck in his first inning as an opener for South Africa. The skipper, Neil Brand, did not miss out on punishing loose deliveries during his stay at the crease but failed to kick on. It was the same story with Raynard van Tonder, as he could not see through that tricky phase before Lunch. After grinding it out for so long in the second session, Zubayr Hamza ran out of patience and gifted his wicket away. Keegan Petersen could not do much, and the visitors were 5 down with just 101 runs on the board. Just as David Bedingham was beginning to get a move on, he popped one off his boot to short leg to be dismissed. Ruan de Swardt did not lose his composure and applied himself really well to hang in there. He found an able alley in the debutant, Shaun von Berg. von Berg was made to work hard for the first run of his Test career but grew in confidence as the innings progressed. The two batters maintained a good tempo, with de Swardt bringing up his maiden Test fifty before the close of play.

SESSION SUMMARY - 63 runs, 29 overs, 2 wickets. A much better session for the hosts, New Zealand who have removed two big wickets and are in solid control of this match. David Bedingham and Zubayr Hamza batted well and showed great application at the crease at the start of the second session. Hamza played a poor shot and will be ruining the missed opportunity, after getting a start. Most of the batters who got in failed to capitalize on the start and gave it away. Ruan de Swardt and David Bedingham have added 26 so far and will need to bat deep to take their side past the 300-run mark.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the second session on Day 1. Tim Southee leads his troops out to the middle and they are followed by the two South African batters. Zubayr Hamza and David Bedingham are all set to resume their innings. Matt Henry will kick things off with the ball in this post-Lunch session. Let's play...
... DAY 1, SESSION 2 ...

On the other hand, South Africa will be disappointed to lose Raynard van Tonder just before Lunch, especially in what was shaping up to be a decent session for them. Considering the grass covering, it looked like a no-brainer to bowl first, but South African skipper Neil Brand surprised everyone by electing to bat first. The visitors faced an early setback when Clyde Fortuin, promoted to open the innings, was dismissed for a golden duck. However, Neil Brand weathered the storm and capitalised on loose deliveries, while Raynard van Tonder played a more conservative role. After Brand fell, van Tonder took the mantle of ticking along and did well. However, he will be kicking himself for having got out while he was looking good. Having successfully overturned an LBW decision early in his innings, Zubayr Hamza has done well to survive and will look to take the innings forward with the newly arrived David Bedingham. Join us back at 6.10 am IST (12.40 am GMT) for the start of the second session.

Neil Wagner is in for a chat. Wagner says that they bowled in the right areas and got the rewards. Adds that there is some assistance on the pitch and they are aware of the conditions. Shares that they need to keep the patience and the results will follow. Closes by saying that it is special to see William O'Rourke doing well in Test cricket and wishes him luck.

SESSION SUMMARY - 64 runs, 27 overs and 3 wickets. End of an absorbing first session, one that belonged to New Zealand! The hosts will be delighted with the proceedings of the session where they were patient and bowled well by and large. Matt Henry gave them the perfect start with a wicket in his first over, thanks to a one-handed stunner from Glenn Phillips. Henry continued to test the batters, as did Tim Southee in the first hour of play. But it was the debutant, William O'Rourke, who broke through for New Zealand, accounting for the South African captain. It did not take long for Neil Wagner to go to his short-ball tactic, and the ploy worked like a charm for him and New Zealand to get rid of the set Rayan van Tonder. With still movement on offer, the hosts will look to continue to chip away with wickets in the second session.

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks break! South Africa opted to bat first on a green wicket and have lost both their openers inside the first hour of play. Clyde Fortuin was dismissed off his first ball post which Raynard van Tonder and Neil Brand added a few but Brand was trapped in front just before the break. New Zealand have been tidy with the ball with Henry and debutant William O'Rourke, among the wickets.  Also, Zubayr Hamza walks out to the crease.

OUT! Given LBW! A big shout and up goes the finger! Raynard van Tonder walks up to his partner and Neil Brand goes for the review! William bowls it with an upright seam from around the wicket, on a good length, on off and middle, Neil Brand does not move his feet much and looks to keep it out with a straight bat. The ball nips back in off the deck and sneaks past the inside edge to rap him high on the back leg. There is nothing on UltraEdge. The Ball Tracking shows that it has pitched in line, the impact is in line and wickets is umpire's call as it is clipping the middle stump. William O'Rourke gets his first Test wicket and what a special moment it is for the debutant. The skipper, Neil Brand walks back dejected who was looking good.

On the flip side, South Africa started well with the ball but the inexperienced showed and failed to contain or put pressure for longer periods. Skipper Neil Brand picked up 8 wickets in the match with his left-arm spin while Dane Paterson also bowled in good areas. Only David Bedingham, Keegan Petersen, and Zubayr Hamza could muster the New Zealand bowling with the bat. Still, South Africa will have to play as a unit and show some resilience against the strong New Zealand side. Can South Africa fare better in the second Test or will New Zealand get an easy win? Let's find out. Toss and team news in a bit. Stay tuned!

New Zealand had some notable performances with Kane Williamson scoring twin tons and Rachin Ravindra making a brilliant double hundred. Kyle Jamieson, Mitchell Santner, and Matt Henry had decent outings with the ball and the Kiwis will hope to put in a similar effort in this Test to make it 2-0.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the 2nd Test between New Zealand and South Africa from  Seddon Park in Hamilton. New Zealand made a mammoth score of over 511 in their first innings to which the Proteas were dismissed for a paltry score of 162, giving the hosts a lead of 349 runs. Tim Southee opted to bat again and gave the visitors a target of 529. South Africans fared better in the 2nd innings but failed to cross the 250-run mark and lost the game by a massive margin. The Black Caps won the first Test convincingly by 281 runs and will be eyeing a clean sweep in this series.
